chapter: Later views and life in Dallas
title: Income from carpentry, music and a pension
summary: Smith earns from roofing and music, draws a pension, and mentions Boston's Army disability.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: As far as your income's concerned, do you make most from building, construction, carpentry...?
Yeah. I make a little bit from carpentry. A little bit. I work a job...
What's your main source of income? Carpentry?
Yeah. And music. Music and carpentry. I put a roof on that house, and we do that by the square...they call it a square. We get $10 a square...
Yeah, putting shingles on top of houses. We haven't done much over the summer.
Has your arthritis caught up on you?
Yeah. I get down. Yeah, come on down and sit down!
Yeah, I can't get too many shingles up there.
Why don't you draw a pension? Or do you?
So why was Boston worried last night? Because I thought he didn't want to be photographed because he wouldn't be...
Well, he just puttin' on. He gets a pretty good income. You know, he went into the Army, and that pays him a pretty good disability. He told me it might have an effect on his checks.
